import math
from gurobipy import *

def solve_problem():
    m = Model("Stochastic_Transportation")
    m.setParam('TimeLimit', 300)

    # --- Data ---
    I = 6  # sources
    J = 11  # destinations
    S = 12  # scenarios
    alpha = 0.9  # confidence level
    max_violations = int(math.floor((1 - alpha) * S))

    supplies = [87, 198, 158, 146, 143, 152]
    recourse_caps = [34, 79, 63, 58, 57, 60]
    base_costs = [[8.61, 9.63, 21.05, 17.48, 10.23, 5.48, 15.56, 6.68, 12.79, 24.62, 9.05], [16.99, 9.15, 9.9, 12.97, 22.06, 16.23, 14.34, 6.02, 24.33, 21.01, 12.21], [24.45, 11.06, 13.36, 17.49, 10.11, 13.0, 24.12, 7.51, 16.54, 6.33, 21.17], [17.73, 11.8, 11.85, 24.95, 5.13, 24.51, 19.17, 14.6, 17.25, 24.06, 17.68], [10.86, 5.0, 15.93, 24.89, 9.44, 12.67, 18.65, 21.41, 6.47, 22.22, 10.6], [13.24, 8.24, 11.33, 12.55, 15.09, 19.17, 15.21, 7.16, 8.26, 11.24, 15.91]]
    recourse_costs = [[17.22, 19.26, 42.1, 34.96, 20.46, 10.96, 31.12, 13.36, 25.58, 49.24, 18.1], [33.98, 18.3, 19.8, 25.94, 44.12, 32.46, 28.68, 12.04, 48.66, 42.02, 24.42], [48.9, 22.12, 26.72, 34.98, 20.22, 26.0, 48.24, 15.02, 33.08, 12.66, 42.34], [35.46, 23.6, 23.7, 49.9, 10.26, 49.02, 38.34, 29.2, 34.5, 48.12, 35.36], [21.72, 10.0, 31.86, 49.78, 18.88, 25.34, 37.3, 42.82, 12.94, 44.44, 21.2], [26.48, 16.48, 22.66, 25.1, 30.18, 38.34, 30.42, 14.32, 16.52, 22.48, 31.82]]
    demand_scenarios = [[29, 32, 35, 22, 27, 21, 24, 13, 38, 21, 28], [20, 22, 50, 22, 38, 20, 18, 9, 32, 17, 26], [25, 40, 35, 15, 33, 21, 26, 12, 39, 19, 23], [28, 22, 46, 17, 26, 21, 24, 9, 55, 18, 16], [25, 33, 41, 18, 33, 19, 21, 13, 33, 20, 17], [19, 37, 44, 23, 42, 20, 22, 13, 37, 14, 21], [17, 38, 42, 18, 26, 18, 15, 12, 49, 19, 15], [29, 29, 39, 24, 43, 16, 22, 13, 37, 13, 16], [27, 23, 36, 20, 31, 18, 21, 10, 38, 21, 22], [29, 31, 56, 25, 37, 27, 27, 14, 32, 16, 21], [29, 28, 31, 16, 39, 25, 23, 10, 35, 16, 20], [17, 22, 39, 23, 26, 22, 23, 14, 49, 22, 22]]

    # Big-M: largest demand * 2
    M = max(demand_scenarios[s][j] for s in range(S) for j in range(J)) * 2

    # --- Variables ---
    # Stage 1: base shipments
    x = {}
    for i in range(I):
        for j in range(J):
            x[(i,j)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Base_S{i}_D{j}")

    # Stage 2: recourse shipments per scenario
    y = {}
    for s in range(S):
        for i in range(I):
            for j in range(J):
                y[(i,j,s)] = m.addVar(lb=0, vtype=GRB.CONTINUOUS, name=f"Recourse_S{i}_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # Violation indicators
    z = {}
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            z[(j,s)] = m.addVar(vtype=GRB.BINARY, name=f"Violate_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # --- Objective: minimize base cost + expected recourse cost ---
    m.setObjective(
        quicksum(base_costs[i][j] * x[(i,j)] for i in range(I) for j in range(J))
        + (1.0 / S) * quicksum(recourse_costs[i][j] * y[(i,j,s)]
                               for s in range(S) for i in range(I) for j in range(J)),
        GRB.MINIMIZE
    )

    # --- Constraints ---
    # C1: Supply (base)
    for i in range(I):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(x[(i,j)] for j in range(J)) <= supplies[i],
            name=f"SupplyBase_S{i}")

    # C2: Supply (recourse per scenario)
    for i in range(I):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(y[(i,j,s)] for j in range(J)) <= recourse_caps[i],
                name=f"SupplyRecourse_S{i}_Sc{s}")

    # C3: Demand chance constraint (SAA)
    for j in range(J):
        for s in range(S):
            m.addConstr(
                quicksum(x[(i,j)] + y[(i,j,s)] for i in range(I))
                + M * z[(j,s)] >= demand_scenarios[s][j],
                name=f"DemandChance_D{j}_Sc{s}")

    # C4: Violation budget per destination
    for j in range(J):
        m.addConstr(
            quicksum(z[(j,s)] for s in range(S)) <= max_violations,
            name=f"ViolationBudget_D{j}")

    m.optimize()
    return m

To: Distribution and Store Operations Leadership
From: Supply Chain Director

Subject: Two-Stage Shipping Plan to Manage Demand Uncertainty and Protect Service Levels

Challenge
We ship from multiple warehouses to multiple stores while facing uncertain customer demand. If we commit too little in advance, we risk stockouts and lost sales; if we commit too much, we incur unnecessary transport and handling costs and tie up inventory in the wrong locations. We need a pragmatic plan that balances cost with service, ensuring customers find products on shelves even when demand spikes.

Two-Phase Approach
To address this uncertainty, we will adopt a two-phase plan:
1) Base shipments (committed in advance): Before demand is known, we allocate standard shipments from warehouses to stores using our contracted lanes and lead times. These shipments must respect available inventory at each warehouse and are designed to cover expected demand efficiently.
2) Emergency shipments (after demand is revealed): Once actual demand materializes, we will place targeted, expedited shipments to cover any shortfalls. These moves are more expensive and operate under separate capacity limits by warehouse, so they should be used sparingly and only where needed.

Reliability Target
Our service-level target requires that each store’s demand be fully met in most forecasted conditions. In other words, stockouts may occur in only a small fraction of the forecast scenarios; beyond that threshold, we must have the right product in the right place. This approach aims to keep shelves stocked for the vast majority of outcomes while acknowledging that eliminating every shortfall is prohibitively costly.

Business Goal
We will identify the most cost-effective plan that:
- Respects warehouse inventory for the base plan and does not exceed emergency capacity limits for the second phase, considered separately by warehouse.
- Ensures each store’s demand is fully satisfied in at least the specified confidence level of forecast scenarios.
- Controls total spend by balancing lower-cost base shipments with the average cost of emergency shipments across all scenarios.

How We Will Execute
- Plan the base shipments to hedge against the most likely demand patterns and utilize the most economical lanes without over-committing inventory at any warehouse.
- Reserve emergency capacity at key warehouses and with priority carriers to address localized spikes, while enforcing limits to avoid runaway costs.
- Evaluate candidate plans against all forecast scenarios to confirm that the service-level target is met for each store and that neither base inventory nor emergency capacity is exceeded.
- Use insights from the scenario evaluation to adjust base allocations (e.g., shift volume to flexible lanes or strategic stores) and refine the emergency playbook (e.g., prioritize critical store-warehouse pairs).

Risks and Mitigations
- Demand mix shifts: Maintain flexible base allocations and ensure emergency capacity is available for high-variability items and stores.
- Carrier constraints: Secure contingency carrier options for emergency moves and confirm lead-time feasibility.
- Data drift: Refresh demand scenarios regularly and adjust the plan as new forecasts arrive.

Next Steps
- Confirm base inventory availability by warehouse and emergency capacity limits.
- Validate shipment lane rates and any accessorials for both standard and expedited moves.
- Finalize forecast scenarios and the service-level target for the upcoming planning horizon.
- Produce the proposed base plan and emergency playbook, review cost and reliability performance across all scenarios, and align on implementation.
